assignment.review_focus: Bluetooth hazard traceability closure check. Three independent agents (Risk Traceability Agent RUN-0003, Software Agent RUN-0004, V&V Agent RUN-0007) have each reported absence of Bluetooth-specific hazard identification, risk control, and verification evidence. This recheck must: (1) search the full corpus for any document referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in the context of PT9L hazard analysis or risk controls; (2) determine whether the Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0) contains a Bluetooth hazard entry and whether any corresponding verification record closes that control; (3) confirm whether the absence is a true gap or whether evidence exists in documents not yet retrieved; (4) assess whether the Bluetooth feature described in the project profile (PT9L transmits temperature to smart device via Bluetooth) is reflected anywhere in the ISO 14971 risk assessment chain. Do not confirm or dismiss the gap — locate and report all available evidence.

mandatory_audit_matrix.check_goal: Verify that risk items, risk controls, and verification activities form a closed traceability chain.

assignment.review_focus: Bluetooth hazard traceability closure check. Three independent agents (Risk Traceability Agent RUN-0003, Software Agent RUN-0004, V&V Agent RUN-0007) have each reported absence of Bluetooth-specific hazard identification, risk control, and verification evidence. This recheck must: (1) search the full corpus for any document referencing Bluetooth, BLE, wireless, or RF in the context of PT9L hazard analysis or risk controls; (2) determine whether the Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0) contains a Bluetooth hazard entry and whether any corresponding verification record closes that control; (3) confirm whether the absence is a true gap or whether evidence exists in documents not yet retrieved; (4) assess whether the Bluetooth feature described in the project profile (PT9L transmits temperature to smart device via Bluetooth) is reflected anywhere in the ISO 14971 risk assessment chain. Do not confirm or dismiss the gap — locate and report all available evidence.

agent_runs.summary: Cross-corpus scan of the PT9L DHF/DMR package reveals 14 candidate consistency issues spanning legacy product residue in active documents, document-number mismatches, unsigned approvals, wrong-product references in BOM and label documents, regulatory applicability conflicts, software diagram contamination, and blood-pressure-specific language appearing in a thermometer DHF.

Hardware audit of PT9L DHF/DMR reveals five substantive consistency findings: a blood-pressure residue phrase in the battery design-verification plan/report, an unresolved BOM conflict between PT3-P10 dual-spring and PT5-M02/M03 separate springs, a total-assembly drawing part-number anomaly (T-Z1-P10 used for two distinct PCBs), missing pass/fail verdicts in multiple T1 sample review checklists, and object-temperature mode accuracy tolerance (±0.2 °C) applied at 30 °C and 45 °C in software test plans despite the design-input accuracy specification only requiring ±0.2 °C for ≥35 °C and ≤42 °C.

The PT9L risk management file set contains multiple traceability chain breaks: the current Risk Management Report references document number PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the active risk set has been revised to V2.0; the active Risk Management Plan carries document number IFT-FXJH01 rather than PT9L-FXJH01; F0013 (PT2L risk plan) internally carries a PT9L-series document number creating a product-identity conflict; no evidence of Bluetooth-specific hazard verification is present in the supplied corpus; DFMEA files (F0071, F0074) are not cross-referenced to the ISO 14971 risk assessment; and the design verification plan/report cites only PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0 while the current report is V2.0, leaving the closed-loop confirmation potentially misaligned.

PT9L software lifecycle audit reveals five substantive findings: BP3L software diagrams appear in the primary PT9L software design folder and T1 sample subfolder without documented shared-component rationale; the software design document version identifier (E0 23.11) cannot be reconciled with the V1.0 identifier cited in test/validation records and BOM; no Bluetooth software requirements or corresponding test/validation evidence is present in the supplied corpus; the IEC 60601-1 test report references software design document DN:PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0 which does not appear in the evidence catalog; and a label review document filed under the active T1 sample folder carries PT2L as the primary product model without justification.

DMR/SOP audit of PT9L design output chain reveals seven substantive findings including a document-number collision on drawing PT9L-F01, a part-number mismatch between the two packaging BOM files, PT3-origin shared-component drawings archived in the PT9L DHF without cross-product justification, an incomplete drawing title-block in a packaging label drawing, a missing outer-carton BOM entry in the primary packaging BOM, a process instruction referencing EBOM by document number without pinning a version, and the design output list carrying blank approval-date fields indicating the formal sign-off record is incomplete.

PT9L DHF regulatory audit identifies eight substantive findings spanning unsigned approval fields across all risk management documents, dual ASTM E1965 version citation without documented transition rationale, inconsistent EN ISO 80601-2-56 and MDR 2017/745 applicability between design input stages, absent 510(k) responsibility agreement for 'andon', biocompatibility reports conducted on PT5 samples rather than PT9L, IFT-prefixed document numbers on active PT9L risk management plans, a historical-folder risk plan (F0013) carrying a PT9L-series document number, and the operation guide referencing MDD rather than MDR for biocompatibility compliance.

PT9L V&V corpus audit reveals five substantive findings: object-temperature accuracy tolerance applied outside the design-input specified range without documented justification; no Bluetooth hazard or functional verification evidence present; blood-pressure residue phrase in battery verification record with no confirmed signed pass verdict in supplied evidence; no verification record references the controlling risk document at V2.0; and the IEC 60601-1 test report's cited software design document (PT9L-RJFA01 V1.0) is absent from the evidence catalog and design output index.

Cross-run synthesis audit of the PT9L DHF/DMR package identifies six substantive regulatory and document-control findings, including one systemic finding covering unsigned approvals across all risk management documents, plus resolution assessments on five specific escalation questions raised by the orchestrator.

llm_output.summary: Full-corpus recheck for Bluetooth hazard traceability in the PT9L risk management chain confirms a true gap: no evidence of Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF hazard identification, risk control, or verification closure exists in any supplied document, while the project profile explicitly states PT9L transmits temperature via Bluetooth, and the active Risk Management Report (PT9L-FXGB01 V2.0, F0020/F0024) contains no retrievable Bluetooth hazard entry in the supplied evidence.
review_notes: The evidence catalog contains two parallel sets of current-version risk documents: F0018–F0020 (IFT-prefixed, Attachment 7 series) and F0022–F0024 (PT9L-prefixed, Attachment 7 series). Both sets were searched exhaustively for Bluetooth/BLE/wireless/RF content; neither set contains any such reference in the supplied evidence lines.

RISK-040 (F0018) confirms the Risk Assessment Report was updated to V2.0 on 2024-05-30 with question list updated per ISO/TR 24971:2020 Annex A; RISK-045 (F0019) confirms the Verification report was updated to V2.0 on 2024-05-30 with hazard sequence alignment. Neither update note references Bluetooth or wireless hazards.

RISK-123 and RISK-124 (F0083, PT9L operation guide) contain an EMC immunity table referencing IEC basic EMC standards and home healthcare environment levels, which is the closest document to wireless/RF content in the corpus, but this is a user-facing document and not a hazard analysis entry.

RISK-127 (F0114, design verification report) and RISK-130 (F0121, design verification plan) both reference EMC testing as a separate verification item from risk management, but neither links EMC or wireless to a specific hazard ID in the ISO 14971 chain.

RISK-138 through RISK-140 (F0243, IEC 62366-1 checklist) reference ISO 14971:2019 compliance via document PT9L-FXGB01 V1.0, not V2.0, consistent with the version mismatch finding from RUN-0003 and RUN-0007.
